submission.justification: Mixture-G1 with a 2.0 mm gas gap achieves the best time resolution of 0.856 ns among all tested configurations. This represents a ~6% improvement over the 2025 simulation result (0.9 ns) and significantly outperforms the other candidate mixtures: Mixture-G3 achieves 1.299 ns at 2.0 mm (52% worse) and Mixture-G2 achieves 2.023 ns at 2.0 mm (136% worse). The 2.0 mm gap is well within the specified 1-3 mm constraint and represents an optimal balance, as both smaller (1.0 mm, 1.5 mm) and larger (2.5 mm, 3.0 mm) gaps show degraded performance. All three candidate mixtures are available from suppliers, have recirculation systems planned, and are compatible with the existing HV system (up to 12 kV), ensuring compliance with laboratory requirements.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible time resolution
requirements.evidence: Mixture-G1 at 2.0 mm gap achieves 0.856 ns time resolution, which is the best among all 15 simulated configurations (3 mixtures × 5 gap sizes).

requirements.requirement: The mixture must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Mixture-G1 is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate gas mixtures in the specifications: 'Mixture-G1: standard fluorinated mixture.'

requirements.requirement: The gas system must comply with the laboratory's environmental and safety policies
requirements.evidence: All three candidate mixtures, including Mixture-G1, are stated to be 'available from suppliers in the required quantities' and have 'closed-loop recirculation system with 90% recovery' planned, indicating compliance with environmental policies. The HV system compatibility is confirmed for all mixtures.
The recommended gas gap of 2.0 mm is within the specified range of 1 to 3 mm.
